moments.name: 14…Bc4
moments.headline: 14…Bc4! The only good move here: every alternative is clearly worse.
points: Skewers the queen: when it moves, the bishop on e2 behind it falls.
The next best move, 14…Bxb3, would drop Black's winning chances from 48% to 31% (+2.21).
14…Bc4 threatens …Bxd3, winning the queen for a bishop, and gets the bishop out of the way of fxe6.
It threatens …Bxd3, winning the queen for a bishop, so White has to spend the next move on it.
White was threatening fxe6, winning a bishop for a pawn. The bishop steps away.

moments.name: 19…Rxc3
moments.headline: 19…Rxc3!! A real sacrifice: Black gives up material and the engine still rates it best.
points: Puts the rook on c3 where it can be taken.
White can take, but after 20.bxc3 Nc5 21.Bxf6 Bxf6 the engine rates it 0.00.
White was threatening Ned5, winning the exchange, picking it up with 20.Nxc7. Rxc3 takes care of it.

why.title: The idea
why.text: 19…Rxc3!! offers the rook on c3. Taking it still leaves Black level.

why.title: What Black gives up
why.text: 19…Rxc3 puts the rook on c3 where it can be taken by the b2 pawn. That's a whole rook on offer.

why.title: What it does instead
why.text: It takes the knight on c3.

why.title: If White takes the rook
why.text: 20.bxc3 is met by 20…Nc5, threatening …Ncxe4, winning a pawn. Then 21…Bxf6 takes the bishop on f6, and 22…Nxe4 takes the e4 pawn. Black is two pawns down: Black holds the balance (0.00). This is White's best try.
